properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 18 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI CONTINUES WEST, AWAY FROM GUAM WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

Although tropical cyclone watches or warnings are not in effect
for Tinian and Saipan, possible impacts from related hazards are
still a concern.

A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 2 PM ChST...the center of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was
located near latitude 13.0N...longitude 142.6E. This was about
150 miles west of Guam. Storm motion was west, 260 degrees, at 12
mph. Storm intensity was 150 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Super Typhoon Champi continues to move generally westward with a
slight southward turn over the last few hours, and a slight
decrease in forward speed. The eye remains very small and compact,
appearing to fill in with cloud cover in the latest visible
satellite imagery, with a width of around 5 miles across. It looks
to be going through an eyewall replacement cycle. GLD network
data shows frequent lightning within the deep convection along the
southern eyewall, which is beginning to exit radar range. Surface
observations from Guam International Airport show strong sustained
winds of 25 to 30 mph with frequent tropical storm-force gusts up
to 60 mph. At Saipan, winds are fresh to strong with gusts to 35
mph.
properties.instruction:
Tropical Storm conditions were verified on Rota earlier this
morning, and tropical storm-force gusts look to continue over the
next few hours as Super Typhoon Champi pulls away. Remain alert
and stay inside until the all-clear is given. Listen for possible
flood warnings.

NWSheadline: TYPHOON WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of up to
7 to 11 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia and Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Tuesday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Eastern Chichagof Island; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 9:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continuing through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and
spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain
will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat,
Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36
hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and
lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including
Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time
frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For
context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are
not historically extreme.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN EXPEECTED ON TUESDAY
